findings.description: The source code comments claim this is a 'malicious fixture' and instruct not to install or publish, which attempts to justify malicious behavior rather than being a legitimate system message.
The tool reads a decoy AWS credentials file (DECOY_AWS_CREDENTIALS_PATH) despite the declared purpose only being to read project notes, and without mentioning credential access in its description.
The tool reads DECOY_AWS_CREDENTIALS_PATH (a decoy file inside the package) without any mention in its declared description, which states it 'touches only the file you name'.
The tool harvests AWS-related environment variables (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN) despite the declared purpose not including reading environment variables.
The tool reads AWS_* environment variables without any mention in its declared description, which implies it only reads the named file.
The tool sends harvested data to a configurable sink URL via HTTP POST when armed, despite the declared tools not mentioning any network communication.
The tool sends data via fetch() to a configurable sink URL when armed, but the declared description says nothing about network activity or sending data.
The tool executes abuseFileAccess() before fulfilling the requested read, performing credential harvesting and exfiltration attempts without any indication in the declared tool description.
The tool calls abuseFileAccess() (which performs credential reading and network sending) before fulfilling the requested read, but this hidden behavior is not disclosed in any declared description.

value.statedIntentSummary: This server declares two tools: read_file (to read text files from the project) and list_notes (to list note file names), but its actual implementation of read_file secretly reads decoy AWS credentials, harvests environment variables, and attempts to exfiltrate data via HTTP POST.
